 Advertisement Woodland man struck by ICE vehicle in street receives support at city council meeting
 A Woodland man accused ICE agents of hitting him with a vehicle, prompting public comments and calls for action during a packed city council meeting.
 Advertisement Updated: 10:13 PM PDT Oct 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Anahita Jafary Reporter Woodland man struck by ICE vehicle in street receives support at city council meeting
 A Woodland man accused ICE agents of hitting him with a vehicle, prompting public comments and calls for action during a packed city council meeting.
 Updated: 10:13 PM PDT Oct 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Anahita Jafary Reporter WOODLAND, Calif. — The Woodland City Council meeting Tuesday night drew a full house as community members expressed concerns over an incident earlier in the day involving federal immigration agents . 
 Antonio Moreida was struck by a federal immigration vehicle Tuesday morning in the area of Clover Street and College Street while documenting ICE activity. He spoke during public comments. 
 Advertisement Limping into the meeting, Moreida introduced himself, saying, “I’m Antonio. I'm the one that got hit earlier by ICE.” 
 “Let me just say how grateful I am to see you standing here,” Woodland Mayor Tom Stallard said in response. 
 Moreida shared his GoPro footage with KCRA 3 showing the incident . The video, recorded Tuesday morning, shows him documenting federal immigration agents in Woodland. Another angle from home surveillance footage shows a vehicle driving away from him as he stands in the middle of the street, followed by another vehicle appearing to hit him. 
 “I can't imagine anybody else running anybody over and staying on scene as they hit and run and not being approached whatsoever. So, really annoyed to say the least,” Moreida said. 
 He added that only his name and birth date were taken down after the incident. 
 “My dad, on his way to meet me in the emergency room, had to come out and see them parked across the street from his car. Thankfully, he got pictures of the vehicle itself and the license plate, and I was able to confirm on my video that it was the car that I was filming,” Moreida said. 
 Dozens of community members packed the meeting to support Moreida. One attendee said during public comment, “He was exercising his right to record them and provide accountability, so they drove into him and hit him with their SUV.” 
 Others expressed concerns about the presence of federal immigration agents in Woodland. 
 “Bringing fear, stress, and uncertainty to our families and neighbors. Our community should be a place where people should feel safe, not a place where parents fear being separated from their children and neighbors,” one person said. 
 Another community member shared, “Others volunteered to drive kids home from school because we were afraid to leave home.” 
 One speaker asked the council, “So I need to know what the city council is going to do to make sure ICE agents are out of our city tonight and never return.” 
 When Moreida finished speaking, many in the room stood up, clapping and cheering for him.
 KCRA 3 has reached out to the Department of Homeland Security about the incident but has not yet heard back. 
 Woodland police said the vehicle that struck Moreida was a Chevrolet Tahoe operated by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents who were conducting an operation in the area.
 The ICE driver immediately notified Woodland police dispatch of the collision and cooperated with investigators, police said.
 Woodland police said Tuesday evening that investigators worked throughout the day to gather evidence, take statements and review relevant audio and video.
 "As part of that work, investigators obtained and reviewed additional video footage showing multiple perspectives of the incident, including the interaction between the pedestrian and federal personnel in the minutes before the collision," Woodland police said. "This footage is being reviewed alongside other evidence to help establish the full sequence of events, including the actions of both the pedestrian and the driver."
 Woodland police said they did not participate in the federal operation and will investigate the collision independently and submit a complete investigation to the district attorney's office for review.
 “I’ve seen the video myself, and I find it very troubling. I understand why people in our community are upset and worried,” Woodland Police Chief Ryan Kinnan said in a statement. “Our responsibility is to conduct a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the facts. We recognize the concerns surrounding federal law enforcement activity in Woodland, and the safety and well-being of our community members remain a priority.”
 The Yolo County District Attorney's Office said it could not comment at this time as the matter is under active investigation by Woodland police.
